356	class _StreamScan:
357	    # Internal incremental engine behind the single-consumption streaming
358	    # entry points (verify_stream, verify_all_stream, heads_stream and
359	    # manifest_stream). The history arrives as an ordered iterable of bytes
360	    # chunks and is validated one chunk at a time, so the caller never has to
361	    # assemble the full bytes: chunks may be cut at any byte boundary
362	    # (mid-UTF-8-sequence, mid-JSON-object or mid-LF), empty chunks are
363	    # allowed, and only the chunks' in-order concatenation is the history.
364	    #
365	    # The verdict nevertheless matches the in-memory entry points for that
366	    # concatenation field for field, because every physical line is rebuilt
367	    # and handed to the same strict decoder and the same tenant/seq/prev/hash
368	    # checks in the same physical order:
369	    #   * physical lines are bounded by exactly one character, the byte 0x0A
370	    #     (LF); a trailing CR stays attached to its line the way _split_lf
371	    #     keeps it, and the empty segment after a final LF is not an extra
372	    #     line (empty buffer at end() yields nothing);
373	    #   * a line's bytes are UTF-8 decoded only once its LF arrives (or at
374	    #     end() for the final LF-less tail), so a multibyte sequence split
375	    #     across chunks is rebuilt before decoding while the first illegal
376	    #     byte is reported on its own physical line -- one plus the number of
377	    #     LFs already processed -- the same bad_line _decode_lines locates;
378	    #   * a completed line is parsed the instant its LF arrives, so the first
379	    #     defective line stops the scan and the streaming entry points never
380	    #     pull another chunk; a valid history is consumed to the end.
381	    #
382	    # all_tenants=False runs verify_bytes' single-tenant scan (records of
383	    # other canonical identities interleave freely and are skipped) and a
384	    # defect is kept as (reason, at), "at" being the expected seq or the
385	    # physical line exactly as _verify_snapshot fills it. all_tenants=True
386	    # runs verify_all_bytes' physical-order scan over every tenant and keeps
387	    # (reason, line, tenant, state_seq): line/tenant/reason back the
388	    # verify_all/heads failure object and state_seq fills the AuditChainStateError
389	    # seq exactly the way _scan_all_chains fills it for manifest_bytes
390	    # (None/None on a line that cannot name a tenant; the record's own seq
391	    # when present as a plain int on a missing-field line, else the expected
392	    # seq). The running byte count and whole-stream sha256 back manifest.
393	    def __init__(self, chain, all_tenants, tenant=None):
394	        self._chain = chain
395	        self._all_tenants = all_tenants
396	        # Single-tenant mode state.
397	        self._key = chain._tenant_key(tenant) if not all_tenants else None
398	        self._expected = 1
399	        self._prev = ZERO
400	        self.count = 0
401	        # All-tenant state: serialized key -> [expected_seq, prev_hash, count]
402	        # and (original_tenant, state) in first-appearance order.
403	        self._states = {}
404	        self._order = []
405	        # Stream mechanics: pending bytes after the last processed LF, the
406	        # completed physical-line count, total consumed bytes, the whole-input
407	        # digest and the first defect reported (None while valid).
408	        self._buffer = b""
409	        self._line_no = 0
410	        self._byte_length = 0
411	        self._hasher = hashlib.sha256()
412	        self._defect = None
413	
414	    @property
415	    def byte_length(self):
416	        return self._byte_length
417	
418	    def feed(self, chunk):
419	        # Fold one bytes chunk into the running stream and validate every
420	        # physical line it completes. Returns the first defect tuple (kept for
421	        # end()) or None while the history stays valid. Bytes are accounted
422	        # for before line validation, which only matters for a successful
423	        # manifest (a defect discards the counters anyway).
424	        if self._defect is not None:
425	            return self._defect
426	        self._byte_length += len(chunk)
427	        self._hasher.update(chunk)
428	        self._buffer += chunk
429	        while True:
430	            idx = self._buffer.find(b"\n")
431	            if idx < 0:
432	                return None
433	            line_bytes = self._buffer[:idx]
434	            self._buffer = self._buffer[idx + 1:]
435	            self._line_no += 1
436	            defect = self._check_line(line_bytes)
437	            if defect is not None:
438	                self._defect = defect
439	                return defect
440	
441	    def end(self):
442	        # Finalize the stream: the bytes still pending after the last LF are
443	        # the final physical line (a history need not end with LF). Returns
444	        # the first defect tuple or None for a fully valid history.
445	        if self._defect is not None:
446	            return self._defect
447	        if self._buffer:
448	            self._line_no += 1
449	            defect = self._check_line(self._buffer)
450	            self._buffer = b""
451	            if defect is not None:
452	                self._defect = defect
453	        return self._defect
454	
455	    def _check_line(self, line_bytes):
456	        # Validate one complete physical line. Strict UTF-8 decoding happens
457	        # here on the line's exact bytes (a split multibyte sequence has been
458	        # rebuilt by feed), then strict standard JSON; neither underlying
459	        # exception ever escapes. The first undecodable/unparseable line is a
460	        # missing-class defect with no determinable tenant.
461	        try:
462	            raw = line_bytes.decode("utf-8")
463	        except UnicodeDecodeError:
464	            return self._bad_line()
465	        try:
466	            item = _strict_loads(raw)
467	        except Exception:
468	            return self._bad_line()
469	        if self._all_tenants:
470	            return self._check_all_item(item)
471	        return self._check_tenant_item(item)
472	
473	    def _bad_line(self):
474	        if self._all_tenants:
475	            return ("missing", self._line_no, None, None)
476	        return ("missing", self._line_no)
477	
478	    def _check_tenant_item(self, item):
479	        # Single-tenant scan, line for line the rules _scan applies: foreign
480	        # canonical identities are skipped, a target record's fields/seq/
481	        # prev/hash are checked from (1, ZERO), and a missing-field defect
482	        # carries the record's own seq when it is a plain int so _verify_snapshot
483	        # reports that seq, else the physical line.
484	        if not isinstance(item, dict) or "tenant" not in item:
485	            return ("missing", self._line_no)
486	        if self._chain._tenant_key(item["tenant"]) != self._key:
487	            return None
488	        if any(k not in item for k in FIELDS):
489	            seq = item.get("seq")
490	            at = seq if isinstance(seq, int) and not isinstance(seq, bool) \
491	                else self._line_no
492	            return ("missing", at)
493	        seq = item["seq"]
494	        if isinstance(seq, bool) or not isinstance(seq, int) \
495	                or seq != self._expected:
496	            return ("sequence", self._expected)
497	        if item["prev"] != self._prev:
498	            return ("digest", self._expected)
499	        if item["hash"] != self._chain._hash(item):
500	            return ("digest", self._expected)
501	        self.count += 1
502	        self._prev = item["hash"]
503	        self._expected += 1
504	        return None
505	
506	    def _check_all_item(self, item):
507	        # Every-tenant physical-order scan, line for line the rules
508	        # _verify_all_snapshot and _scan_all_chains share. The state is looked
509	        # up before the field check, so a missing-field line fills the
510	        # manifest state error's seq with its own plain-int seq or the
511	        # expected one, exactly _scan_all_chains' rule; the verify_all/heads
512	        # failure object instead reports the physical line as "at".
513	        if not isinstance(item, dict) or "tenant" not in item:
514	            return ("missing", self._line_no, None, None)
515	        tenant = item["tenant"]
516	        key = self._chain._tenant_key(tenant)
517	        state = self._states.get(key)
518	        if state is None:
519	            state = [1, ZERO, 0]
520	            self._states[key] = state
521	            self._order.append((tenant, state))
522	        expected, _prev, _count = state
523	        if any(k not in item for k in FIELDS):
524	            seq = item.get("seq")
525	            state_seq = seq if isinstance(seq, int) \
526	                and not isinstance(seq, bool) else expected
527	            return ("missing", self._line_no, tenant, state_seq)
528	        seq = item["seq"]
529	        if isinstance(seq, bool) or not isinstance(seq, int) \
530	                or seq != expected:
531	            return ("sequence", self._line_no, tenant, expected)
532	        if item["prev"] != state[1]:
533	            return ("digest", self._line_no, tenant, expected)
534	        if item["hash"] != self._chain._hash(item):
535	            return ("digest", self._line_no, tenant, expected)
536	        state[0] += 1
537	        state[1] = item["hash"]
538	        state[2] += 1
539	        return None
540	
541	    def verify_all_result(self, with_hash=False):
542	        # Project the successful scan into verify_all_bytes' result shape
543	        # (with_hash=True adds each tenant's verified tail hash for heads).
544	        tenants = []
545	        for tenant, state in self._order:
546	            entry = {"tenant": tenant, "count": state[2]}
547	            if with_hash:
548	                entry["hash"] = state[1]
549	            tenants.append(entry)
550	        return {"ok": True, "tenants": tenants}
551	
552	    def manifest_result(self):
553	        # Project the successful stream into the version-1 manifest: the
554	        # byte length and sha256 describe the exact concatenated input bytes
555	        # and tenants follow physical first-appearance order with original
556	        # tenant value, verified count and last-record hash.
557	        return {
558	            "version": MANIFEST_VERSION,
559	            "byte_length": self._byte_length,
560	            "byte_sha256": self._hasher.hexdigest(),
561	            "tenants": [
562	                {"tenant": tenant, "count": state[2], "hash": state[1]}
563	                for tenant, state in self._order
564	            ],
565	        }

570	    # single validation body both the bytes and chunked offline range entries

572	    # the chain tail it continues is named by expected_prev, never by the
573	    # target log -- so no AuditChain path is ever probed. Every physical line
574	    # must be a record of the one declared canonical JSON tenant identity
575	    # carrying exactly the five FIELDS keys; seqs must run start_seq,
576	    # start_seq+1, ... with the first prev equal to expected_prev, and each
577	    # hash is recomputed with the existing algorithm. The mechanics are
578	    # _StreamScan's exactly: bytes accumulate behind LF-only physical-line
579	    # boundaries, strict UTF-8 decoding waits for the completed line, chunks
580	    # may be cut at any UTF-8/JSON/LF position, and the first defective
581	    # completed line stops feed so the caller never pulls another chunk.

585	    # end_seq}); a record of another canonical tenant identity violates the
586	    # single-tenant segment contract and is raised as _ForeignTenant (surfaced
587	    # as ValueError), the same rule the import scans use, and wins by
588	    # physical line order over a later chain defect. After all lines, an empty
589	    # segment or a declared end_seq the records stop short of is the missing
590	    # verdict "declared range missing its tail".
591	    def __init__(self, chain, tenant, start_seq, end_seq, expected_prev):
592	        self._chain = chain
593	        self.tenant = tenant
594	        self.start_seq = start_seq
595	        self.end_seq = end_seq
596	        self._key = chain._tenant_key(tenant)
597	        self._expected = start_seq
598	        self._prev = expected_prev
599	        self.count = 0
600	        self._buffer = b""
601	        self._line_no = 0
602	        self._defect = None
603	
604	    def feed(self, chunk):
605	        # Fold one bytes chunk into the running segment and validate every
606	        # physical line it completes, exactly the _StreamScan loop: a
607	        # completed line is checked the instant its LF arrives, so the first
608	        # defective line ends the scan and a chunked caller never requests
609	        # another chunk. Returns the kept verdict dict or None while valid.
610	        if self._defect is not None:
611	            return self._defect
612	        self._buffer += chunk
613	        while True:
614	            idx = self._buffer.find(b"\n")
615	            if idx < 0:
616	                return None
617	            line_bytes = self._buffer[:idx]
618	            self._buffer = self._buffer[idx + 1:]
619	            self._line_no += 1
620	            try:
621	                self._check_line(line_bytes)
622	            except _ForeignTenant:
623	                raise
624	            if self._defect is not None:
625	                return self._defect
626	
627	    def end(self):
628	        # Finalize the segment: the bytes pending after the last LF are the
629	        # final physical line (a segment need not end with LF), then the
630	        # declared interval must be covered exactly. Returns the kept verdict
631	        # dict or None when the segment fully verifies.
632	        if self._defect is not None:
633	            return self._defect
634	        if self._buffer:
635	            self._line_no += 1
636	            pending, self._buffer = self._buffer, b""
637	            self._check_line(pending)
638	            if self._defect is not None:
639	                return self._defect
640	        if self.count == 0:
641	            self._defect = self._fail("missing", self.start_seq)
642	            return self._defect
643	        if self.end_seq is not None and self._expected <= self.end_seq:
644	            # Records ran out before the declared closed interval: the first
645	            # seq the segment owes but does not contain locates the missing
646	            # tail.
647	            self._defect = self._fail("missing", self._expected)
648	            return self._defect
649	        return None

651	    def _fail(self, reason, at):

653	            "ok": False,
654	            "reason": reason,
655	            "at": at,
656	            "tenant": self.tenant,
657	            "start_seq": self.start_seq,
658	            "end_seq": self.end_seq,

667	        # and a recomputed current hash. The first problem in physical order

673	            raw = line_bytes.decode("utf-8")
674	        except UnicodeDecodeError:
675	            self._defect = self._fail("missing", self._line_no)

677	        try:
678	            item = _strict_loads(raw)
679	        except Exception:
680	            self._defect = self._fail("missing", self._line_no)
681	            return
682	        if not isinstance(item, dict) or "tenant" not in item:

684	            return

707	            return
708	        if item["prev"] != self._prev:
709	            self._defect = self._fail("digest", self._expected)
710	            return
711	        if item["hash"] != self._chain._hash(item):
712	            self._defect = self._fail("digest", self._expected)

714	        self.count += 1
715	        self._prev = item["hash"]
716	        self._expected += 1

718	    def result(self):

730	            "count": self.count,

735	class AuditChain:
736	    def __init__(self, path):
737	        self.path = Path(path)
738	
739	    @contextlib.contextmanager
740	    def _dir_lease(self):
741	        # Auxiliary exclusive lease on the containing directory itself. It
742	        # never carries data bytes; its only job is to make the moment a data
743	        # file first appears indivisible relative to a conditional append
744	        # that is allowed to create the file only on its winning branch.
745	        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
746	        dfd = os.open(self.path.parent, os.O_RDONLY)
747	        try:
748	            fcntl.flock(dfd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
749	            yield
750	        finally:
751	            fcntl.flock(dfd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
752	            os.close(dfd)
753	
754	    @contextlib.contextmanager
755	    def _write_lease(self):
756	        # Exclusive lease for one read-modify-append. The same open file
757	        # description carries the lock, the history read and the final append:
758	        # flock is tied to that description, so the lease cannot be silently
759	        # lost to a second open of the path, and the bytes appended are the
760	        # ones computed from the bytes just read. A fresh fd per call makes
761	        # flock genuinely exclude both other processes and other threads.
762	        # The creating open happens inside the directory lease, so a
763	        # conditional append probing a not-yet-existing path cannot race the
764	        # file's first appearance (see append_if_head); the lease is released
765	        # again before blocking on the data file, so it never serializes
766	        # unrelated chains in the same directory for a write's duration.
767	        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
768	        with self._dir_lease():
769	            f = open(self.path, "a+b")
770	        try:
771	            fcntl.flock(f.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX)
772	            f.seek(0)
773	            yield f
774	            # Flush while the lease is still held, so the lock is released
775	            # only after the full record has reached the kernel file.
776	            f.flush()
777	        finally:
778	            # Closing the description also releases the flock.
779	            f.close()
780	
781	    def _read_snapshot(self):
782	        # One complete, self-consistent read-only view, protected by a shared
783	        # lease on the data file itself. The file is opened O_RDONLY, so a
784	        # verify never creates the path: when it does not exist yet that is a
785	        # legitimate pre-append view and yields empty bytes. Under the shared
786	        # lock no append can be mid-flight, so the snapshot is always the full
787	        # state either before or after some append, never a partial record.
788	        try:
789	            f = open(self.path, "rb")
790	        except FileNotFoundError:
791	            return b""
792	        try:
793	            fcntl.flock(f.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_SH)
794	            return f.read()
795	        finally:
796	            fcntl.flock(f.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_UN)
797	            f.close()
798	
799	    @staticmethod
800	    def _split_lf(text):
801	        # Physical lines are bounded by exactly one character: the byte 0x0A
802	        # (LF), so a CRLF sequence is still one line -- the trailing CR stays
803	        # attached to its line and strict JSON accepts it as line-ending
804	        # whitespace. No other character ends a record: U+0085, U+2028,
805	        # U+2029 and a bare CR are valid UTF-8 content of the current line
806	        # and are handed to strict JSON (which keeps the three Unicode
807	        # separators as ordinary string content and rejects a raw CR inside

820	        # Split the raw JSONL bytes into LF-bounded physical lines while
821	        # treating the first illegal UTF-8 byte as a hard, locatable stop
822	        # point. Returns (lines, bad_line): lines are the complete physical
823	        # lines preceding any corruption (all lines when the bytes are valid
824	        # UTF-8), bad_line is the 1-based LF physical line number of the
825	        # first undecodable line or None. A bad line is never yielded, even
826	        # if the bytes before the illegal byte looked like complete JSON:
827	        # callers scan the preceding complete lines first, so an earlier
828	        # JSON/sequence/digest error still takes priority. Empty bytes are
829	        # zero physical lines, not one blank one.
830	        if not data:

835	            # start is the offset of the first byte that cannot be decoded;

837	            # count LF bytes only, so the bad line's number is one plus the
838	            # number of LFs before that offset.
839	            start = exc.start

841	            cut = data.rfind(b"\n", 0, start) + 1  # start of the bad line
842	            prefix = data[:cut]
